system: You are a helpful assistant. Make sure your answer addresses every request in the message.
message:
Morning. I'm coordinating final interviews for our data analyst role on Thursday and need help with a few things.

Can you suggest a friendlier subject line for the invitation than "Interview Invitation"?

Each interview is 45 minutes and must be with both panellists, Ana and Ben, in the room. Ana is free 09:00 to 12:30 and again 14:00 to 15:30. Ben is free 10:00 to 15:00. We need 15 minutes between interviews for the panel to write up notes. Chloe can only do the morning (she has to start before 12:00). Dev can't start before 11:00. Elif has to be finished by 14:45 to catch a train. Can you give me times for all three that work?

Could you also give me a short paragraph describing the day that I can paste into the email? And list three questions the candidates might ask us that we should have answers ready for. What format should the panel use to score, a shared online form or individual paper sheets? And what's a kind way to tell an internal applicant that they didn't make the final shortlist? Finally, could you suggest a short checklist for the room setup (water, printed CVs, that sort of thing) so I don't forget anything on the morning?
response:
# Thursday Final Interviews: Planning Pack

## 1. Friendlier subject line

**"Next step: let's meet! Data Analyst final interview"**

Other options:
- "You're through to the final round: Data Analyst interview"
- "Invitation to meet the team: Data Analyst final interview"

## 2. Interview schedule

Ana and Ben are both free **10:00–12:30** and **14:00–15:00**. The morning window fits two interviews with the 15-minute write-up gap. The afternoon window fits one.

| Candidate | Time | Constraint check |
|---|---|---|
| **Chloe** | **10:00–10:45** | Morning, starts before 12:00 ✅ |
| *Write-up* | 10:45–11:00 | |
| **Dev** | **11:00–11:45** | Starts at 11:00 ✅ |
| *Write-up* | 11:45–12:00 | Panel free until 14:00 |
| **Elif** | **14:00–14:45** | Finishes by 14:45 ✅ |
| *Write-up* | 14:45–15:00 | Fits inside Ben's availability ✅ |

**Backup option:** Chloe 10:00, Elif 11:00–11:45, Dev 14:00–14:45. This gives Elif more time for her train if she'd like it.

**Date check:** today is Thursday 12 November. If you mean next Thursday, that's **19 November**. Worth stating the full date in the email.

## 3. Paragraph for the email

> Thank you for your interest in the Data Analyst role. We're delighted to invite you to a final interview on Thursday [date] at [time]. You'll meet Ana and Ben from the team for a relaxed, 45-minute conversation about your experience, how you approach working with data, and what you're looking for in your next role. There will also be plenty of time for you to ask us questions about the team and how we work. There's nothing you need to prepare in advance, but please bring along any examples of your work you'd like to talk through. We're based at [address]; when you arrive, just ask at reception for [name]. If you need any adjustments to make the interview accessible for you, please let us know. We're looking forward to meeting you!

Remove or edit the "nothing to prepare" line if you're setting a task.

## 4. Questions candidates might ask

1. **"What does a typical week look like, and what would I be working on in the first 3–6 months?"** Have a concrete project or two ready.
2. **"What tools and data stack does the team use?"** For example SQL, Python or R, Power BI or Tableau, your data warehouse, and how mature the data infrastructure is.
3. **"What are the next steps, and when will I hear back?"** Agree a decision date and the salary/benefits position beforehand so Ana and Ben answer consistently.

## 5. Scoring format

**I'd recommend a shared online form** (e.g. Microsoft Forms or Google Forms), with a few conditions:
- Each panellist **scores independently, during or straight after the interview, before discussing.** This avoids one person's view anchoring the other's.
- Use the **same criteria and a defined scale** (e.g. 1–4 with short descriptors) for every candidate.
- Include a free-text box for evidence, so scores are backed by what the candidate actually said.
- Results collate automatically, which makes comparison and record-keeping easy.

Paper sheets are fine if the panel won't have laptops in the room. Since they'll be taking notes on paper anyway, that's a valid choice. What matters most is **independent scoring against agreed criteria**, not the medium.

## 6. Telling an internal applicant they didn't make the shortlist

**Tell them in person or by video call first, before anyone else knows the shortlist.** Then follow up in writing. Suggested wording:

> Hi [Name], thank you so much for applying for the Data Analyst role. I know it takes real commitment to put yourself forward, and we genuinely appreciated it. It was a very strong field, and on this occasion we haven't been able to take you through to the final round. This was a difficult decision, and it isn't a reflection of the value you bring to the team. I'd really like to offer you some feedback on your application and talk about what development or experience could strengthen you for similar roles in future. Would you be up for a chat next week? Thanks again, and please don't hesitate to come and talk to me in the meantime.

Make sure the feedback offer is real: have specific, constructive points ready, and follow through.

## 7. Room setup checklist

**Day before**
- [ ] Room booked for the full day (10:00–15:00), including the write-up slots
- [ ] Reception and security told candidate names and arrival times
- [ ] Interview questions and scoring criteria agreed with Ana and Ben

**Morning of**
- [ ] Printed CVs/applications for each panellist, in interview order
- [ ] Printed question sheet and scoring sheets (or form link open on laptops)
- [ ] Spare pens and notepaper
- [ ] Water jug and glasses, including one for the candidate
- [ ] Room temperature, lighting and chairs arranged (avoid a "panel vs. candidate" barrier if possible)
- [ ] "Interview in progress – please do not disturb" sign on the door
- [ ] Tech checked if needed (screen, HDMI, Wi-Fi guest login for portfolios)
- [ ] Tissues and a clock visible to the panel, so they can keep time without checking phones
- [ ] Phones on silent
- [ ] Someone assigned to meet each candidate at reception
- [ ] Waiting area identified so candidates don't bump into each other
- [ ] Your contact number handy in case a candidate is running late

Good luck on Thursday!
